treasury_auctions.narrative: Today's 7-Year Note auction — pending at the last check — has now settled cleanly: dealer take of just 10.84% is the lowest of the three auctions in this week's cluster, indirect (foreign/institutional) demand held at 53.72%, and the bid-to-cover of 2.50 sits comfortably in the normal range. Combined with the 2-Year and 5-Year Notes that settled earlier this week (both also showing low dealer takedown), this is now three consecutive clean auctions. NY Fed's primary-dealer net Treasury inventory continues its 3-week decline (most recent available print, Aug 12) — dealers are not stuck holding unwanted supply. SOFR is trading 1bp below IORB, a normal funding reading with no repo stress. None of the three transmission flags are triggered. This reads as 'duration repricing' territory (absorption healthy, dealer take low, repo normal) rather than 'Treasury intermediation stress' — even with yields drifting slowly higher this week.
